Only the legacy file and an orphan interface remain; no active contract implements ICrossChainArk.
staleClaims.evidence: packages/core-contracts/src/contracts/arks/legacy/CrossChainArk.sol.old (entire file); interface packages/chain-bridge/src/interfaces/ICrossChainArk.sol:12 has no active implementer

staleClaims.currentTruth: withdrawAndTransfer(uint amount, BridgeTypes.BridgeOptions calldata options) exists only in the retired legacy file; the function is absent from all active source.

staleClaims.claim: Keepers queue and execute rebalances from the buffer to one or more CrossChain Arks targeting other chains
staleClaims.currentTruth: The queue/execute mechanism (Ark._board storing pendingTransferParams, keeper-called executeTransferAssets) lived in the removed CrossChainArk; the documented hub-to-satellite fleet rebalancing flow has no active implementation. BufferArk and FleetCommander deposit-to-buffer remain (FleetCommander.sol:279,316).

docs.notes: Bridge-layer half of the doc remains accurate: BridgeRouter (packages/chain-bridge/src/router/BridgeRouter.sol), Stargate/LayerZero adapters (packages/chain-bridge/src/adapters/), CrossChainRegistry, registry-first validation, only-local-router trust + adapter peer-mapping check on deliver (BridgeRouter.sol:121-131,495,505), pause/governance controls (BridgeRouter.sol:597-604), and nonReentrant guards all confirmed. The fleet-level half (CrossChain Ark, FleetProxy, keeper withdraw flow) describes contracts deprecated on 2026-02-10; the doc was last touched 2025-09-09 (commit 43ac4ab83).

staleClaims.claim: Steps 3-9 and the sequence diagram: keepers queue transfers into the CrossChain Ark, the Ark calls the BridgeRouter, the destination router calls FleetProxy which deposits into the local fleet
staleClaims.currentTruth: Both endpoint contracts (CrossChainArk, FleetProxy) were deprecated and moved to .sol.old legacy files in commit 8c0beb15d (2026-02-10); the documented keeper-led rebalancing flow cannot run against current active source. The router-level steps (executeTransferAssets, adapter forwarding, deliver) still match BridgeRouter.sol.

No function named queueTransfer ever existed; queuing happened inside the Ark's _board(amount, executeTransferParams) hook during fleet rebalance, which decoded ExecuteTransferParams + BridgeOptions and stored them as pendingTransferParams (emitting PendingTransferQueued only on execution).

staleClaims.claim: 'A registered executor (keeper) executes the queued transfers' / 'Router execution is gated by onlyAuthorizedExecutor (keepers must be registered executors)'
staleClaims.currentTruth: Misattributes the executor requirement. The Ark's executeTransferAssets() was gated by the onlyKeeper access-manager role (ProtocolAccessManaged.sol:151), not the registry. The router's onlyAuthorizedExecutor checks msg.sender — the Ark contract itself — and _validateOriginator requires params.originator == msg.sender, so the contract registered via CrossChainRegistry.registerExecutor must be the Ark/Proxy, not the keeper address.

staleClaims.claim: Reconciliation cues: Ark inflightAssets / lastRemoteAssetBalance; FleetProxy latestIncomingTransferId / fleetBalance notification; keepers call FleetProxy.withdrawAndTransfer(amount, options)
staleClaims.currentTruth: All of this state and these functions exist only in the legacy .sol.old files (the logic itself matched the doc when active: router best-effort updateInflightAssets is still live at BridgeRouter.sol:293-312, but no active contract holds the state).

docs.notes: Every name and constant checked against the legacy implementations matched (the doc was accurate for the system as built), and router-side claims (executeTransferAssets signature with ExecuteTransferParams+BridgeOptions, onlyAuthorizedExecutor gating, adapter peer verification on deliver, Stargate failedComposes fail-safe) are still confirmed in active code. But the document's subject — the CrossChainArk/FleetProxy rebalancing flow — describes a removed feature.

staleClaims.claim: 'route deliveries to recipients (e.g., FleetProxy)' and 'For fleet rebalancing, the recipient is the destination chain's FleetProxy'
staleClaims.currentTruth: FleetProxy was deprecated and removed from active source (legacy/FleetProxy.sol.old, commit 8c0beb15d); the router delivers to any ICrossChainReceiver recipient, but no FleetProxy recipient exists in current code.

docs.notes: All router/adapter claims confirmed against active code: 1% fee buffer ((baseFee*101)/100, BridgeRouter.sol:249-254); explicit adapter selection via BridgeOptions.specifiedAdapter (BridgeTypes.sol:26-32, quote reverts NoSuitableAdapter at BridgeRouter.sol:474); validAdapter rejects unregistered/unsupported (BridgeRouter.sol:98-105); token pull from originator==msg.sender then forceApprove adapter (BridgeRouter.sol:283-291,188-190); best-effort IInflightAssetTracking notification (BridgeRouter.sol:293-312); deliver gated by onlyRegisteredAdapter with PEER_RELATIONSHIP check for (sourceChainId, adapter) (BridgeRouter.sol:79-82,121-131,505,523); adapter capabilities estimateFee/transferAsset/sendMessage/readState (IBridgeAdapter.sol:78, IAssetAdapter.sol:51, IMessageAdapter.sol:67,80); adapter-side excess refund (StargateAdapter.sol:353-364); registry/pause governance (registerAdapter/removeAdapter onlyGovernor BridgeRouter.sol:581-594, pause onlyGuardianOrGovernor:597, unpause onlyGovernor:602); nonReentrant on entry points. One nuance worth noting: the peer-mapping check is intentionally skipped for READ_STATE deliveries (BridgeRouter.sol:530-549), which the doc's blanket 'verifies adapter peer relationships during delivery' does not mention.

staleClaims.claim: 'Keepers must be registered executors to invoke the router via the Ark'
staleClaims.currentTruth: Wrong actor: onlyAuthorizedExecutor (CrossChainConfigManaged.sol:35-38, backed by CrossChainRegistry.isAuthorizedExecutor) checks the router's msg.sender, i.e. the originating contract (Ark/FleetProxy), which must equal params.originator (BridgeRouter.sol:188-190,269). Keepers were authorized via the onlyKeeper access-manager role on the (now removed) Ark, not via registry executor registration.

staleClaims.claim: Source-side validation by 'the CrossChain Ark' and destination-side validation by 'the FleetProxy' (sections describe live contracts)
staleClaims.currentTruth: Both contracts are deprecated legacy (.sol.old). The described validation logic did match the legacy code exactly (Ark _getTargetProxy via registry; FleetProxy msg.sender==bridgeRouter() check at FleetProxy.sol.old:229-233 and isValidCrossChainPair check at 308-340), but no active contract performs these checks today.

unverifiable: 'Registry state must be identical across all participating chains' — operational/deployment requirement, not enforceable or checkable in code (the registry only enforces that each relationship touches the deployment chain via InvalidChainRelationship)
docs.notes: Registry API claims all confirmed precisely against active code: governance-only register/unregister (CrossChainRegistry.sol:88-94,106-110); constants PEER_RELATIONSHIP / ARK_FLEET_RELATIONSHIP / EXECUTOR_RELATIONSHIP as keccak256 of their names (CrossChainRegistry.sol:53-57, ICrossChainRegistry.sol:136-147); pseudocode signatures match exactly — getRelationshipByTarget(sourceContract, relationshipType, targetChainId) returning CrossChainRelation with .targetContract (ICrossChainRegistry.sol:300-304,22-28) and isValidCrossChainPair(source, target, uint16 sourceChainId, uint16 targetChainId, relationshipType) (ICrossChainRegistry.sol:272-278); router-side deliver enforcement of onlyRegisteredAdapter + peer relationship (BridgeRouter.sol:495,505); uint16 chain IDs throughout.

staleClaims.claim: Precondition: 'Keeper addresses are registered as authorized executors in the CrossChainRegistry on the source chain'
staleClaims.currentTruth: Incorrect actor: registry executor registration (registerExecutor, CrossChainRegistry.sol:178) must cover the contract that calls BridgeRouter (the Ark/Proxy, since onlyAuthorizedExecutor + originator==msg.sender bind the caller), while keeper EOAs needed the keeper role from the ProtocolAccessManager (onlyKeeper).

staleClaims.claim: Rebalancing runbook: queue transfers from Buffer Ark to CrossChain Ark(s); reconciliation via Ark inflightAssets / lastRemoteAssetBalance and FleetProxy latestIncomingTransferId / notifySourceChain(...)
staleClaims.currentTruth: The CrossChainArk and FleetProxy contracts holding all of this state and these functions were deprecated and moved to legacy .sol.old files in commit 8c0beb15d (2026-02-10); none of the named state variables or notifySourceChain exist in active source.

BridgeRouter pause/unpause confirmed (pause onlyGuardianOrGovernor, unpause onlyGovernor); FleetProxy pause/unpause exists only in the retired legacy implementation (onlyGuardian/onlyGovernor) and the orphan IFleetProxy interface.

docs.notes: Still-accurate items: registry relationship management (registerRelationship/unregisterRelationship/registerAdapterPeer onlyGovernor, CrossChainRegistry.sol:88-110, ICrossChainRegistry.sol:365-370); adapter fail-safe and governance recovery (StargateAdapter failedComposes mapping at StargateAdapter.sol:53-57 and manualRecovery onlyGovernor at 641-648); asset recovery for stuck native/ERC20 on the router (BridgeRouter.recoverAssets, BridgeRouter.sol:607-625). The runbook's central procedures, however, operate on contracts that no longer exist in active code.

summary: Audited 5 cross-chain docs (83 claims) against packages/chain-bridge/src and packages/core-contracts/src. The bridge layer the docs describe is fully intact and matches precisely: BridgeRouter (1% fee buffer via (fee*101)/100, onlyAuthorizedExecutor gating, explicit BridgeOptions.specifiedAdapter selection, token pull + forceApprove, best-effort IInflightAssetTracking notification, onlyRegisteredAdapter deliver with PEER_RELATIONSHIP peer-mapping check, governance adapter registry, pause/unpause, recoverAssets, nonReentrant), CrossChainRegistry (onlyGovernor register/unregister, ARK_FLEET/PEER/EXECUTOR relationship constants, exact getRelationshipByTarget and isValidCrossChainPair signatures with uint16 chain IDs), and Stargate/LayerZero adapters (estimateFee/transferAsset/sendMessage/readState, refund handling, failedComposes fail-safe, manualRecovery). However, the fleet-level endpoints — CrossChainArk and FleetProxy — were deprecated and moved to .sol.old legacy files in commit 8c0beb15d (2026-02-10), five months after the docs' last update (43ac4ab83, 2025-09-09); functions/state the docs cite (withdrawAndTransfer, notifySourceChain, inflightAssets, lastRemoteAssetBalance, latestIncomingTransferId, the queue/execute flow) exist only in legacy files, with orphan interfaces (ICrossChainArk, IFleetProxy) and no active implementations. A cross-cutting inaccuracy in three docs: registry 'authorized executor' registration applies to the contract calling the router (the Ark/Proxy itself, since originator must equal msg.sender), not keeper addresses, which were gated by the access-manager keeper role. Verdicts: BRIDGE_ROUTER_AND_ADAPTERS and REGISTRY_AND_SECURITY partially-stale; OVERVIEW and OPERATIONS_PLAYBOOK stale; REBALANCING_FLOW obsolete.
